mechanism.summary: Compile capture-free ordinary RegExp patterns once into an ordered backtracking program whose execution uses predecoded atoms and a reusable explicit choice stack instead of repeatedly rediscovering groups, quantifiers, atoms, and temporary match-state vectors.
mechanism.generality: Admission depends only on immutable RegExp syntax and flags: no capturing groups, backreferences, lookarounds, or unsupported nullable loops; supported literals, classes, escapes, anchors, word boundaries, non-capturing groups, alternation, and greedy or lazy quantifiers use the program. It contains no workload name, source path, input length, checksum, iteration count, or expected-result condition. Every unsupported pattern falls back before observable matching to the unchanged general matcher.
semantic_risks: preserving ECMAScript leftmost-first, alternation, greedy, and lazy backtracking priority
preserving Unicode code-point and WTF-16 code-unit advancement through the existing atom and class semantics
preserving anchors and word-boundary behavior with multiline and ignore-case flags
rejecting all captures, named groups, backreferences, lookarounds, and nullable unbounded loops before the optimized executor is selected
preserving RegExp test, exec, match, replace, and lastIndex result protocol through the unchanged RegexpMatch boundary

profile_evidence.source: macOS sample 2026-07-29 /tmp/qjs-tagcloud-repeat-current.sample; 25x wrapper of the hash-verified SunSpider string-tagcloud source. The current runtime source is identical to af4a65a1 outside documentation-only commits. Of 4,319 main-thread samples, 1,655 are under PreparedRegexp::match_input, with native RegExp replace, match_pattern_first, and simple_atom_boundaries below it.
profile_evidence.shared_cost: Capture-free JSON-validation and replacement patterns repeatedly enter the generic matcher, which reparses atoms and quantifiers and materializes simple-atom boundary vectors for every candidate start.
